tasks.spec:
You are a MEASUREMENT scout for the OBE podcast repo at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. You may READ any file in that repo and run ffmpeg/ffprobe/python, but you MUST NOT modify, create, or delete anything inside it: no source/test/config edits, no git commit/checkout/stash, no orchestrator or driver runs, and no writes anywhere under /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast (including episodes/). Capture `git -C /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast status --porcelain` at the start and end into probe.log; they must match. Your only writable location is your scratch task directory. No network. No publish/send/deploy. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do NOT invoke any LLM from the pipeline. Subscription/OAuth only, zero API spend. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp everywhere. numpy is available for correlation work; if it is not importable, say so and use a pure-python correlation over decimated audio rather than skipping the measurement.

WHERE THIS SITS: episode 2026-06-10-fred-cho is the hands-off proof episode. Four render defects were fixed today (decoded-sample certification, -shortest mux truncation, per-contribution audio PTS continuity, and an earlier map/frame issue). As of tonight the angle_segments gate clears ALL 102 planned segments and the program renders: a 1.0GB angle_switched.mp4 plus its .boundaries.json sidecar. THE RENDER IS NOT THE QUESTION ANY MORE. The pipeline now halts at the transfer / publishable_render gate:
  FAIL AV_SYNC_DIVERGENCE mode=av_anchors anchor_s=945.728 mapped_source_anchor_s=1517.494333 audio_source_s=1517.551333 av_divergence_ms=+57.000 threshold_ms=40.000 audio_confidence=0.405
and an earlier line in the same run reported anchor_s=1891.055333 mapped_source_anchor_s=2569.621999666666 audio_source_s=2569.811499666666 av_divergence_ms=+189.500.

THE ARTIFACTS TO MEASURE (all READ-ONLY; copy nothing into the repo):
  edited program: /tmp/claude-1000/-mnt-d-drive-repos-loop-factory/b41a49f1-2844-4cf6-ba25-2991cffeabad/scratchpad/e104-shadow/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/angle_switched.mp4
  its boundary map: the same path with .boundaries.json appended (edited_start_s / edited_end_s / source_start_s / source_end_s per piece)
  source composite: /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite.mp4 (video 2842.200s / 85267 frames at 30fps; audio 2919.601s at 48kHz)

THE GATE YOU ARE JUDGING: server/pipeline/media_gates.py validate_transfer (around line 796) and _validate_transfer_impl (around line 826). Read them properly. Note the design already in place: in av_anchors mode an anchor whose audio match confidence is below min_audio_confidence=0.4 is UNMEASURABLE and counts neither pass nor fail, and the gate fails closed only when fewer than min_strong_anchors=3 measurable anchors agree. The failing anchor scored 0.405, five thousandths ABOVE that floor. So either the render really is 57ms out of sync at that point, or a barely-trusted anchor was mis-located and its 57ms is noise.

YOUR JOB: measure the TRUE audio offset at those anchor points INDEPENDENTLY of the gate's own matcher, and say which it is.
1. For each anchor, use the boundary map to convert the edited timestamp to its source timestamp yourself, and show that arithmetic.
2. Extract a window of audio (a few seconds, centred on the anchor) from BOTH the edited program and the composite with ffmpeg, decode both to mono 48kHz s16le, and CROSS-CORRELATE them to find the lag that maximises correlation. Report the lag in milliseconds and the normalised correlation peak (0..1) so the reader can judge how trustworthy each measurement is. A peak near 1.0 with a clean single maximum is a real measurement; a low, flat, or multi-peaked correlation means the anchor is not locatable and its 'offset' is meaningless.
3. Do this for AT LEAST 3 anchors, and you MUST include both anchors the gate reported (edited 945.728s and edited 1891.055s). Add at least one anchor early in the program (before the first content cut) as a control: if the offset is ~0 early and grows later, that is accumulating drift; if it is scattered and uncorrelated with position, it is measurement noise; if it is a constant offset everywhere, it is a fixed lag.
4. State what the offsets do as a function of position, with the numbers.

DELIVERABLES in your scratch dir:
1. offsets.json -- {"anchors": [{"edited_time_s": ..., "mapped_source_time_s": ..., "measured_offset_ms": ..., "correlation_peak": ...}, ...], "verdict": "<one sentence committing to real drift vs mis-located anchor, and why>"}. correlation_peak must be a 0..1 normalised quality value (the receipt checks the range).
2. probe.log -- every command and raw output, plus the before/after git status.
3. report.md with these EXACT headings: '## What was measured', '## Drift or measurement', '## Root cause', '## Fix design', '## Proof command', '## Risks'.

FIX DESIGN CONSTRAINTS. If the audio really is late by 57ms at that point, the fix belongs wherever that lag is introduced (name the stage with evidence) and NOT in the gate. If instead the anchors are mis-located, the honest fix is about anchor SELECTION or confidence handling, and you must argue precisely why the current 0.4 floor admits an untrustworthy anchor, using your measured correlation peaks as evidence -- 'raise the floor until it passes' with no measurement behind it is FORBIDDEN and you must say so if tempted. Likewise do not propose widening threshold_ms, and do not propose skipping the gate. This gate is the last thing standing between a rendered program and a published episode, so a fix that makes it stop looking is worse than the bug. Engage explicitly with min_audio_confidence in your report.
tasks.verified: Both anchors the gate failed on were re-measured by direct cross-correlation of the edited program against the source composite, with per-anchor correlation quality and an early-program control, so the report can say with evidence whether the render carries real A/V drift or the gate trusted an anchor it could not locate
